artists.biography:
65daysofstatic (also known by the abbreviations 65dos, 65days, or simply 65) are an instrumental post-rock and math rock band from Sheffield, England comprising Paul Wolinski, Joe Shrewsbury, Rob Jones and Simon Wright. The band has released five studio albums: The Fall of Math, One Time for All Time, The Destruction of Small Ideas, We Were Exploding Anyway, and Silent Running.

Initially, the band interspersed heavy, progressive, guitar-driven instrumental sections with live drums and off-beat sampled drums akin to those of Aphex Twin, although since their second album they have developed their work to include keyboard parts.

perplexity.description:
Released in 2019 on Superball Music, replicr, 2019 is the eighth studio album by British electronic rock band 65daysofstatic. The album is a complex, genre-defying work that blends aggressive electronic textures, post-rock dynamics, and experimental sound design. Characterized by its dark, tense atmosphere, replicr, 2019 moves fluidly between moments of ambient introspection and explosive rhythmic assaults, with tracks like “stillstellung” and “popular beats” exemplifying the band’s mastery of juxtaposing calm and chaos. The album’s 14 tracks are structured with short interludes and transitions, creating a restless, ever-evolving soundscape that refuses to settle, while standout pieces such as “five waves” and the reflective closer “trackerplatz” showcase the band’s ability to craft both visceral and melodic moments.

In the context of 65daysofstatic’s discography, replicr, 2019 continues the band’s tradition of pushing musical boundaries and redefining their sound with each release. Departing from the brighter optimism of earlier albums, this record delves into murkier, more anxious territory, reflecting themes of technological unease and existential dread. Critics widely praised the album for its intricate textures, emotional depth, and immersive quality, with many highlighting its suitability for focused, uninterrupted listening. While some reviewers noted the brevity of certain tracks as a limitation, the album was generally regarded as a bold and compelling addition to the band’s catalog, solidifying their reputation as innovators in the electronic and progressive rock scenes.
